questions.question: Which bin/console commands install and activate a plugin I just created?
questions.answer:
To install and activate a newly created plugin, you would use the following two commands from your Shopware project root directory:

```bash
bin/console plugin:install --activate SwagBasicExample
```

This command installs the plugin and activates it.

If you need to refresh the list of plugins after creating or installing a new one, you can also use:

```bash
bin/console plugin:refresh
```

questions.question: How can I scaffold a new plugin from the CLI, and which files are always generated?
questions.answer:
To scaffold a new plugin from the CLI, you use the `bin/console plugin:create` command. The following files are always generated by default when using this command without any additional options:

- `composer.json`
- The base plugin class (usually named after your namespace)
- `config.xml`
- `.gitignore`
- PHPUnit setup for testing

You can also use the `--static` flag to create the plugin in `custom/static-plugins` instead of `custom/plugins`. For more details, refer to the [Creating Plugins guide](creating-plugins.md).

questions.question: Where does the config.xml for a plugin settings page go and what is the minimum it has to contain?
questions.answer:
The `config.xml` for a plugin settings page should be placed inside the `src/Resources/config/` directory of your plugin. The minimum structure required in the `config.xml` file includes at least one `<card>` element with a `<title>` and at least one `<input-field>`. Here is an example of what this minimal configuration might look like:

```xml [PLUGIN_ROOT/src/Resources/config/config.xml]
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<config xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
        xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/shopware/shopware/trunk/src/Core/System/SystemConfig/Schema/config.xsd">
    <card>
        <title>Minimal configuration</title>
        <input-field>
            <name>example</name>
        </input-field>
    </card>
</config>
```

questions.question: What classes and service tags do I need to create a scheduled task in a plugin?

retrieved.heading: Registering a scheduled task in the DI container

claims.claim: To create a scheduled task in a plugin, you need to define two main classes: `ScheduledTask` and its handler (`ScheduledTaskHandler`).
The `ScheduledTask` class needs to extend from `Shopware/Core/Framework/MessageQueue/ScheduledTask/ScheduledTask`.
The `ScheduledTask` class must implement two methods: `getTaskName()` and `getDefaultInterval()`.
The task name should include a vendor prefix for uniqueness.
The `getDefaultInterval()` method returns the interval in seconds.
The `ScheduledTaskHandler` class needs to extend from `Shopware/Core/Framework/MessageQueue/ScheduledTask/ScheduledTaskHandler`.
The `ScheduledTaskHandler` class must implement the `run()` method where you define what should happen when the scheduled task runs.
Both classes need to be registered in your plugin's `services.php` file with appropriate service tags: `shopware.scheduled.task` for the task and `messenger.message_handler` for the handler.
The registration code uses `ContainerConfigurator` to define services with specific arguments for the handler.

questions.question: How do I create a database migration for my plugin and which method should contain the schema changes?
questions.answer:
To create a database migration for your plugin, you can use the `database:create-migration` command. Here's an example of how to generate a new migration file:

```bash
$./bin/console database:create-migration -p SwagBasicExample --name ExampleDescription
```

The generated migration will have two methods: `getCreationTimestamp()` and `update()`. The `update()` method is where you should put your schema changes for the plugin. Shopware runs this method automatically when the plugin is installed or updated.

**Note:** There is no automatic rollback of migrations; remove plugin data in the plugin lifecycle `uninstall` method when appropriate.

questions.question: How do I give my plugin its own log channel?
questions.answer:
[1] To configure your plugin with a unique log channel, you need to add the configuration for this channel in your `src/Resources/config/packages/monolog.yaml` file. Here's how you can set up a new log channel named 'my_plugin_channel' and direct it to a rotating file handler:

```yaml
# src/Resources/config/packages/monolog.yaml
monolog:
  channels: ['my_plugin_channel']

my_plugin_channel:
  type: rotating_file
  path: '%kernel.logs_dir%/my_plugin_%kernel.environment%.log'
  level: error
  channels: [ 'my_plugin_channel']
```

questions.question: How can I make the API return only a few fields of an entity, and how is that different from includes?
questions.answer:
To make the API return only a few fields of an entity, you can use `partial data loading`. This feature allows selecting specific fields to be returned by the API. Here's how it works:

```json
{
    "fields": [
        "id",
        "name"
    ]
}
```
This example would return only the `id` and `name` fields of an entity.

The difference between `partial data loading` and includes is that `includes` works as post-output processing. It loads the complete entity on the backend and then filters it, whereas `partial data loading` works already at the database level. This means the database only loads the requested fields, not the entire entity.

For more details, refer to [Partial Data Loading](https://developer.shopware.com/docs/guides/development/integrations-api/partial-data-loading.html) and [Search Criteria](https://developer.shopware.com/docs/guides/development/integrations-api/search-criteria.html#parameters).
